title: Ubuntu Terminal Foundations
moduleObjectives: Navigate the Linux filesystem confidently using `pwd`, `ls`, and `cd`
Create, copy, move, rename, and delete files and directories from the terminal
Read and edit files from the terminal using `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `less`, `nano`, and output redirection
Update an Ubuntu system and install packages with `apt` using `sudo`
Interpret and modify file permissions and ownership with `chmod` and `chown`
Diagnose basic network connectivity and DNS with `ping`, `curl`, `dig`, and `ss`
Inspect running processes and service status with `ps`, `top`, `systemctl`, and `journalctl`
Chain commands with pipes and `grep`, and manage users and groups in preparation for the docker group

lessons.title: Setup Check
lessons.objective: Verify that the Ubuntu environment is course-ready by checking the OS release, internet connectivity, DNS resolution, and sudo access.

lessons.title: Where Am I?
lessons.objective: Navigate the filesystem without hesitation using `pwd`, `ls`, `cd` with absolute paths, `cd -`, and the `~` home shortcut.

lessons.title: Making Things
lessons.objective: Create the ~/docker-course working directory and practice creating, copying, moving, renaming, and deleting files and directories with `mkdir`, `touch`, `cp`, `mv`, and `rm`.

lessons.title: Looking Inside Files
lessons.objective: Create, read, and edit files from the terminal using `echo` with `>` and `>>` redirection, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `less`, `wc -l`, and `nano`.

lessons.title: Sudo and System Updates
lessons.objective: Perform a full system update with `sudo apt update`, `sudo apt upgrade -y`, and `sudo apt autoremove -y`.

lessons.title: Installing Software
lessons.objective: Install and verify the Docker prerequisite packages (curl, wget, git, htop, tree, ca-certificates, gnupg) using `sudo apt install`.

lessons.title: Permissions Drills
lessons.objective: Read permission strings and change file permissions and ownership using `chmod` in symbolic and numeric forms and `chown` with sudo.

lessons.title: Networking Drills
lessons.objective: Diagnose network readiness for Docker Hub using `ip a`, `ping`, `curl`, `ss -tuln`, and `dig`.

lessons.title: Processes and Services
lessons.objective: Inspect running processes and service status using `ps aux`, `top`, `htop`, `systemctl`, `journalctl`, `uptime`, `free -h`, and `df -h`.

lessons.title: Pipes and Grep
lessons.objective: Chain commands together with pipes and search files using `grep` (including -v, -i, and -r), `wc -l`, `cut`, `sort`, and `uniq`.

lessons.title: User and Group Setup
lessons.objective: Inspect user and group membership with `id` and `groups`, add a user to a group with `sudo usermod -aG`, and refresh group membership with `newgrp`.

lessons.title: Final Checkpoint
lessons.objective: Demonstrate every skill from the module by running the cumulative command drill from memory to prove the environment is ready for Docker installation.

quiz.question: What does the command `cd -` do?
options: Takes you to your previous directory and prints where it took you
Takes you to your home directory
Moves up one level to the parent directory
Takes you to the root of the filesystem
quiz.feedback: `cd -` switches to the directory you were in previously and prints the path it moved to, letting you bounce between two locations.

quiz.question: What does the `-p` flag do in `mkdir -p projects/web/app`?
options: Prompts for confirmation before creating each directory
Creates the full nested path in one command and does not error if directories already exist
Sets read and write permissions on the new directories
Prints each directory name as it is created
quiz.feedback: `mkdir -p` creates all missing parent directories in the path and succeeds silently even if the path already exists, which makes it safe to rerun.

quiz.question: When redirecting `echo` output into a file, what is the difference between `>` and `>>`?
options: `>` appends to the file while `>>` overwrites it
They behave exactly the same
`>` only works on new files and `>>` only works on existing files
`>` overwrites the file while `>>` appends to it
quiz.feedback: A single `>` replaces the file's contents while `>>` adds to the end, which is why using `>` by mistake can destroy a file.

quiz.question: What does `sudo apt update` do?
options: Installs all available package upgrades
Removes packages that are no longer needed
Downloads the latest list of available software packages
Upgrades Ubuntu to the next release version
quiz.feedback: `apt update` only refreshes the package list so the system knows what versions are available; `apt upgrade` is what actually installs the upgrades.

quiz.question: According to the lesson, why is the `gnupg` package installed before Module 02?
options: It handles encryption keys, which is needed for Docker's GPG key
It provides the certificates required for secure HTTPS connections
It is a better process viewer than top
It displays directory structures visually
quiz.feedback: The lesson installs gnupg because it handles encryption keys, and the Docker installation in Module 02 requires it to work with Docker's GPG key.

quiz.question: After running `chmod 755 hello.sh`, what permission string does `ls -la` show for the file?
options: -rw-r--r--
-rwxr-xr-x
-rwxrwxrwx
-rw-rw-r--
quiz.feedback: 755 means the owner gets rwx (7) while group and everyone else get r-x (5), which displays as -rwxr-xr-x.

quiz.question: Which command shows the ports currently listening on your machine?
options: `ip a`
`dig +short hub.docker.com`
`ss -tuln`
quiz.feedback: `ss -tuln` lists listening TCP and UDP sockets with their local addresses and ports, such as port 22 for SSH.

quiz.question: What does `systemctl is-active ssh` print when the SSH service is running?
options: enabled
running
active
online
quiz.feedback: `systemctl is-active` gives a one-word status, and a running service reports `active`; `enabled` is what `systemctl is-enabled` reports for boot startup.

quiz.question: What does `echo "hello world" | grep -v hello` output?
options: hello world
world
Nothing, because `grep -v` prints only lines that do NOT match
An error, because -v is not a valid grep flag
quiz.feedback: The -v flag inverts the match so grep prints non-matching lines, and since the only input line contains "hello" it is excluded.

quiz.question: In this module, running `sudo usermod -aG docker $USER` fails. Why?
options: The user does not have sudo access yet
The docker group does not exist yet; it is created when Docker is installed in Module 02
usermod can only be run while logged in directly as root
The -aG flags must come after the username
quiz.feedback: The lesson runs the command as a rehearsal and it fails with "group 'docker' does not exist" because the docker group is only created when Docker is installed in Module 02.
